title: Establishment and analysis of artificial neural network diagnosis model for coagulation-related molecular subgroups in coronary artery disease.
summary: The study used feature selection and an artificial neural network to distinguish two coagulation-related molecular subgroups in coronary artery disease, then characterized their immune and pathway differences. This is a molecular-subgroup analysis, not evidence of clinical benefit.
ai_technology: Random-forest/LASSO feature selection and an artificial neural network were used to classify coagulation-related CAD molecular subgroups.
organization: Department of Cardiology, Dongguan Hospital of Integrated Chinese and Western Medicine Affiliated to Guangzhou University of Traditional Chinese Medicine, China; Shenzhen Traditional Chinese Medicine Hospital, Guangzhou University of Chinese Medicine, China; Beijing University of Chinese Medicine Shenzhen Hospital (Longgang), China

evidence.tested: The analysis reports two molecular subgroups with differing immune and pathway profiles, based on coagulation-related gene features.
evidence.unknown: The authors used training and validation datasets; the result is a computational subgroup distinction and does not establish clinical utility or causal mechanisms.
evidence.ai_role: A learned classifier enabled a distinction between coagulation-related CAD molecular subgroups and comparison of their molecular profiles.

source_review.scope: Primary Frontiers full text and Europe PMC full-text record; publication date checked against primary metadata.
